sop_modules.name: Setup — Landscape/Hardscape Protection, Fixture Masking, HVAC Cover, Vehicle/Driveway Protection, Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Full setup module for exterior fiber cement siding repaint. Landscape perimeter protection (LF-based along house where landscape is adjacent — catches scraping debris and rinse water runoff in addition to overspray). Hardscape walk/patio protection. Light fixture and HVAC masking. Vehicle/driveway overspray protection (RP-specific — occupied home context, spray_backroll only). Equipment setup: spray_backroll rig (airless sprayer + 18-inch backroll frame + roller covers) or brush/roll kit per application method. Window/door protection is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs in window/door specs.

tasks.name: Landscape Perimeter Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent to siding work area. Measured in linear feet along foundation/siding line. RP scope includes scraping debris and rinse water runoff containment beyond NC overspray coverage. brush_roll: edge tarps at base. spray_backroll: full tarp width over plantings. RRP: upgrades to 6-mil poly via ext_rrp_containment zone.
tasks.notes: Shared zone with SF_TRIM_EXT_RP — first spec in elevation sequence owns setup. Cross-spec deduplication rule U-004. RP emphasis: catches scraping debris in addition to overspray.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_LANDSCAPE_PROTECT (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

tasks.name: Hardscape Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy drop cloths and plastic over walkways, patios, and driveways adjacent to siding. Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic areas. Upgrade to full_cover for spray_backroll or RRP.
tasks.notes: Shared zone with SF_TRIM_EXT_RP — cross-spec deduplication rule U-004.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_HARDSCAPE_PROTECT (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

tasks.name: Fixture and Utility Masking
tasks.description: Mask exterior light fixtures, house numbers, utility panels, hose bibs. Bag and tape HVAC units if adjacent. RP: all fixtures are installed and operational — masking is mandatory.
tasks.notes: RP: all fixtures are installed and operational. Complete coverage mandatory for both spray_backroll and brush_roll.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_FIXTURE_MASK (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

tasks.name: Extended Landscape Overspray Protection (Spray Only)
tasks.description: Extended overspray protection for landscape areas beyond the perimeter edge tarps. Required when spray_backroll application creates wider drift zone than brush_roll. Full tarp coverage over plantings in the drift zone.
tasks.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: Extended overspray zone beyond perimeter. Spray_backroll only. Follows wood siding RP pattern.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Vehicle/Driveway Overspray Protection
tasks.description: Deploy poly sheeting and drop cloths over vehicles, driveway surfaces, and garage areas adjacent to siding work zone. RP-specific — occupied home context. Vehicles and driveway require protection from spray_backroll overspray and scraping debris.
tasks.notes: RP-SPECIFIC: Occupied home context. Spray overspray on vehicles is a liability. Shared zone with other exterior RP specs.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Spray/Backroll Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Configure airless sprayer, hoses, tips for fiber cement siding. Stage 18-inch backroll frame, roller covers (3/8 nap smooth, 1/2 nap textured), roller trays. Stage materials. 2-person operation: sprayer + backroller.
tasks.notes: FIXED time per session. Includes backroll equipment staging (roller covers, trays) in addition to spray setup. Slightly longer than NC spray-only setup (~50 min vs 45 min).
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_EQUIPMENT_SETUP_SPRAY — adds backroll equipment staging

tasks.name: Brush/Roll Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Stage brushes, rollers, trays, and materials. Fallback method for <750 SF, occupied-adjacent, or high wind.
tasks.notes: FIXED time per session. Same method as NC. Rate unchanged.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_EQUIPMENT_SETUP_BRUSH — re-keyed, unchanged method

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape/hardscape protection first → Fixture/HVAC masking → Vehicle/driveway protection (spray only) → Equipment setup last. All setup complete before assessment begins.

sop_modules.name: Condition Assessment — Visual Inspection, Adhesion Test, Chalk Test, Moisture Probe, Mildew/Efflorescence Scan, Caulk Assessment
sop_modules.description: RP-specific multi-point assessment module. Results drive downstream task activation: substrate state assignment, primer selection, prep intensity, condition scale. Visual condition inspection per elevation (map cracking, peeling, chalking, fading). ASTM D3359 adhesion test at representative sections. Chalk rub test (exterior-specific — most common FC degradation mode). Moisture probe at joints and water damage areas. Mildew/algae scan (especially north/shaded elevations). Efflorescence scan (FC-specific). Caulk assessment per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol on all joint types. FIXED time per elevation. 100% RP_NEW tasks.

tasks.name: Visual Condition Inspection — All Siding Surfaces Per Elevation
tasks.description: Scan all siding field surfaces per elevation from ground and at working height. Map cracking, peeling, adhesion failure, chalking, fading, weathering damage, paint film buildup, butt joint condition, and caulk failure zones. Assign substrate state (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT / SS_EXT_CHALKING / SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT / SS_EXT_PEELING) per worst-state-wins rule. Photograph defects. Document scope of scraping, feathering, and treatment needed.

quality_notes.QT2: Quick ground-level scan. Note obvious defects.
quality_notes.QT3: Standard visual with work light, document visible defects per elevation.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan with raking light, photograph all defect areas, per-elevation assessment.

tasks.notes: Per-elevation FIXED task (~15-20 min per elevation). Exterior siding exposed to UV, rain, thermal cycling — wider range of failure modes than interior. Height access may limit inspection at upper stories.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Adhesion Test (ASTM D3359 Cross-Hatch Tape Test)
tasks.description: Perform cross-hatch tape test per ASTM D3359 at representative sections per elevation. Test at minimum 2 locations per elevation (field area + butt joint area). Critical for fiber cement — chalking surfaces may appear sound but chalk layer prevents bonding. Results determine if full prime or skip-prime path applies.
tasks.notes: Per-elevation FIXED task. Pass result + SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT = skip prime (ROUND_FCRP_2FINISH or ROUND_FCRP_1FINISH). Fail result = full prime required regardless of visual condition.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Chalk Test (White Cloth Rub)
tasks.description: Rub clean white cloth across painted siding surfaces to detect chalking. Exterior-specific test — chalking is a UV degradation failure mode that does not occur on interior surfaces. Grade: none (clean cloth), light (faint transfer), moderate/heavy (obvious powdery transfer). Moderate/heavy chalking triggers chalk-binding primer path. Test on each elevation — south/west elevations chalk faster.
tasks.notes: Per-elevation FIXED task. Chalking is the MOST COMMON FC siding RP degradation mode. Moderate/heavy chalk drives SS_EXT_CHALKING state and triggers SYS_EXT_FCRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Moisture Probe — Joints, Butt Joints, Water Damage Areas
tasks.description: Moisture meter reading at siding-to-trim junctions, butt joints, and areas with visible water damage. FC itself does not absorb moisture through the face, but water intrusion behind siding at failed joints is detectable. Moisture content >15% at substrate edge = STOP WORK for coating on that area until moisture source is resolved and material dries to <12%.
tasks.notes: Per-elevation FIXED task. High moisture indicates failed flashing, WRB breach, or caulk failure allowing water behind siding. FC's cementitious matrix does not absorb through the face but edges and joints are vulnerable.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Efflorescence Scan (FC-Specific)
tasks.description: Inspect siding surfaces for white crystalline salt deposits — efflorescence from moisture evaporating through the cementitious matrix. FC-specific condition not found on wood siding. Classify: surface deposits (dry brush + neutralize + prime), active/recurring (STOP — moisture source must be resolved). Check under paint film for blistering caused by sub-surface efflorescence.
tasks.notes: Per-elevation FIXED task. FC-specific assessment. Active/recurring efflorescence = STOP WORK until moisture source resolved. Surface efflorescence triggers TSK_FCRP_EFFLORESCENCE_TREAT in prep.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Caulk Assessment — 'Think Like a Water Drop' Protocol
tasks.description: Inspect all existing caulk joints per elevation using 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol: trace water path from top of elevation downward, assess every joint where water could enter. Inspect siding-to-trim junctions (corner boards, frieze, window/door casings), butt joints on lap siding, and siding-to-foundation transitions. Classify: intact (paint over), cracked/separated (remove + re-caulk), fully failed (remove all + clean + re-caulk). Document total LF requiring replacement.

quality_notes.QT2: Quick scan of major joints — note obvious failures.
quality_notes.QT3: Comprehensive assessment of all joint types. Document LF requiring replacement.
quality_notes.QT4: Critical assessment of every joint. Full LF documentation with defect photographs.

tasks.notes: Per-elevation FIXED task. FC siding has significantly more caulk joints than wood siding. Caulk failure is a primary trigger for FC siding repaint. Results drive TSK_FCRP_CAULK_REMOVE and TSK_FCRP_CAULK_APPLY_NEW in prep.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Condition inspection first → Chalk test → Adhesion test → Moisture probe → Efflorescence scan → Caulk assessment. Assessment results determine which prep and prime tasks activate downstream. ~20-30 min per elevation depending on size and condition.

sop_modules.name: Prep — Low-Pressure Rinse, Mildew Treatment, Degloss/Scuff, Scrape/Feather, Chalk Remediation, Efflorescence Treatment, Caulk Remove/Replace, Dust/Debris Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Combined prep module for all surface preparation, cleaning, and caulk work. Low-pressure rinse (400-600 PSI max — NO power washing on FC). Mildew/algae biocide treatment. Condition-driven surface prep: degloss/scuff (sound paint), scrape/feather (failing/peeling). Chalk remediation for SS_EXT_CHALKING. Efflorescence treatment (FC-specific — dry brush + neutralize). Caulk removal and replacement per 'Think Like a Water Drop' results. Dust and debris cleanup. Condition modifiers: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x on prep tasks. RRP modifier: 2.0x on tasks involving paint disturbance (rare for FC). CRITICAL: High-pressure power washing is PROHIBITED on fiber cement — strips existing paint, damages embossed texture profiles, forces water behind wall assembly.

tasks.name: Low-Pressure Rinse (400-600 PSI Max)
tasks.description: Clean siding surface with garden hose and soft-to-medium bristle brush, or gentle power rinse at 400-600 PSI maximum with 40-60 degree wide fan tip. Removes weathering dirt, chalk residue, mildew, loose paint flakes, and surface contaminants. TSP solution at QT4 for stubborn dirt/chalk. HIGH-PRESSURE POWER WASHING IS PROHIBITED on fiber cement — strips existing paint, damages embossed texture profiles (cedarmill, roughsawn), forces water behind wall assembly through butt joints and J-channels. Allow 24-48 hr dry time before coating.

quality_notes.QT2: Basic rinse to remove loose dirt and debris.
quality_notes.QT3: Full low-pressure rinse per elevation. Allow 24 hr dry time.
quality_notes.QT4: Full low-pressure rinse with TSP solution. Allow 24-48 hr dry time.

tasks.notes: Per-elevation FIXED task. CRITICAL departure from wood siding RP (which uses 1000-1500 PSI power wash) and exterior trim RP (500-1000 PSI). Cross-spec deduplication rule U-004: if rinse already performed by another spec on same elevation, skip.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_WASH_LOW_PRESSURE — RP purpose (weathering dirt vs construction dust), TSP at QT4

tasks.name: Mildew/Algae Biocide Treatment
tasks.description: Apply biocide/mildewcide solution to mildew or algae-affected siding areas. Common on north-facing and shaded elevations in humid climates. Allow 10-15 min dwell/kill time per product directions. Rinse with low-pressure water. Allow dry before priming. Must treat before any coating — mildew will grow through new paint.
tasks.notes: RP-SPECIFIC. Condition assessment drives activation. FC's dense non-porous surface resists mold penetration but surface mildew is common. If heavy, may require second treatment.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Degloss/Scuff Existing Paint
tasks.description: Chemical degloss (liquid sander wipe-on) or mechanical scuff (150-180 grit) on all previously painted siding surfaces. Creates adhesion profile for primer or finish coat. Chemical degloss preferred for hard-to-sand areas. For GOOD condition (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT), degloss/scuff may be the only prep task needed.

quality_notes.QT3: Thorough degloss — chemical or mechanical on all accessible surfaces.
quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss with adhesion verification on all surfaces.

tasks.notes: Skip for SS_EXT_PEELING (full scrape renders degloss redundant). Skip for SS_EXT_CHALKING (chalk remediation + chalk-binding primer path). Condition modifier applies: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_SCUFF_SAND — RP degloss existing paint vs NC bare wood sanding

tasks.name: Scrape Failing Paint and Feather Edges
tasks.description: Scrape all failing, peeling, flaking, or loose paint from siding field surfaces. Feather-sand all scrape edges with 80-100 grit to create smooth transition — no visible ridge. Carbide scraper for exterior paint buildup. Collect scraping debris for cleanup (RRP: into containment). Non-negotiable feathering at all tiers.

quality_notes.QT2: Remove all failing paint, feather edges — no visible ridge at 10 ft.
quality_notes.QT3: Comprehensive scrape + near-invisible feathering at 6 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Critical scrape + perfect feathering — no ridge at 3 ft.

tasks.notes: Condition-driven intensity: FAIR = moderate scraping (1.5x); POOR = heavy scraping (2.0x). RRP doubles scraping time (wet methods required — 2.0x). After scraping, inspect for exposed bare FC → requires alkali-resistant primer on bare areas.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Chalk Remediation (Pre-Primer Surface Treatment)
tasks.description: Pre-treat chalking siding surfaces before chalk-binding primer application. Low-pressure rinse (already done) loosens heavy chalk; follow with chemical chalk remover on stubborn areas. Wipe and verify — white cloth test should show minimal residual chalk after treatment. Residual chalk will be bound by chalk-binding primer. This is the most common FC siding RP prep scenario.
tasks.notes: Exterior-specific. Chalking is the most common FC siding RP degradation mode — UV binder breakdown on dense cementitious substrate. Chalk-binding primer (SYS_EXT_FCRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND) follows this task.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Efflorescence Treatment (FC-Specific)
tasks.description: Dry brush to remove surface efflorescence deposits. Neutralize with dilute acetic acid (vinegar) or commercial efflorescence remover if heavy. Rinse and allow dry. Apply alkali-resistant primer over neutralized area. FC-specific condition — white crystalline salt deposits from moisture evaporating through cementitious matrix. CRITICAL: If efflorescence is active/recurring, STOP painting until moisture source is addressed.
tasks.notes: FC-SPECIFIC RP task. Not found in wood siding RP. Surface efflorescence: treat and paint. Active/recurring efflorescence: resolve moisture source first (failed flashing, WRB breach, drainage issue).
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Remove Failed Caulk from Joints
tasks.description: Remove cracked, shrunk, and failed caulk from all joint types identified during caulk assessment. Siding-to-trim junctions (corner boards, frieze, window/door casings), butt joints on lap siding, and siding-to-foundation transitions. Cut out failed sections with utility knife. Clean joint to bare substrate for maximum adhesion of new caulk. Collect debris.
tasks.notes: Separated from caulk replacement for rate tracking. FC siding has significantly more caulk joints than wood siding. Condition drives volume: GOOD = near-zero, FAIR = moderate, POOR = extensive.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW (split from NC TSK_FCSD_CAULK_JOINTS — NC applies fresh only; RP assesses + removes + replaces)

tasks.name: Apply New Caulk to Cleaned Joints
tasks.description: Apply exterior-grade paintable caulk (polyurethane or siliconized acrylic) to all cleaned and bare joints. Tool smooth for professional appearance. Use continuous bead — no gaps. Do NOT caulk lap siding field butt joints unless previous caulk existed and was removed (maintaining original joint treatment). Allow 2-4 hr cure before overcoating per product TDS.

quality_notes.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead. Precision tool smooth. Inspect for uniformity.

tasks.notes: Major scope for FC siding RP. Typical residential: 200-500 LF of caulk joints per project. 10.3 oz tube covers ~20-25 LF of 1/4-inch bead. Typical project: 8-15 tubes. 2-4 hr cure before overcoating.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW (split from NC TSK_FCSD_CAULK_JOINTS)

tasks.name: Prep Dust and Debris Cleanup
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust, scraping debris, chalk residue, efflorescence residue, and caulk removal debris from all surfaces before coating. Tack cloth, compressed air, or light brush. RRP: all debris collected into containment for lead-safe disposal.
tasks.notes: RP generates more debris than NC (sanding dust + scraping debris + chalk residue + caulk debris). All surfaces clean before primer/topcoat application.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_DUST_CLEANUP — RP adds scraping debris + chalk residue + caulk debris

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Low-pressure rinse → Dry time (24-48 hr) → Mildew treatment (if present) → Efflorescence treatment (if present, FC-specific) → Scrape/feather (failing/peeling areas) → Degloss/scuff (sound areas) → Chalk remediation (chalking areas) → Caulk removal → Caulk replacement → Caulk cure (2-4 hr) → Dust/debris cleanup. RINSE MUST PRECEDE ALL OTHER PREP.

sop_modules.name: State-Driven Primer Application — Chalk-Binding, Spot Alkali-Resistant, Acrylic Stain-Block, Full Prime
sop_modules.description: State-driven + substrate-driven primer module. SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT: skip prime when adhesion verified (no bare areas). SS_EXT_CHALKING: chalk-binding primer full surface. SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare FC + acrylic stain-block primer on remaining. SS_EXT_PEELING: full alkali-resistant primer on all exposed bare FC areas + acrylic stain-block full surface. When scraping exposes bare FC (pH 13.0), alkali-resistant primer is MANDATORY to prevent saponification. spray_backroll is primary method; brush_roll is fallback.

tasks.name: Chalk-Binding Primer — Full Surface Application
tasks.description: Apply chalk-binding primer (SW PrimeRx Peel Bonding Primer, Zinsser Peel Stop, or equivalent) to full siding surface for SS_EXT_CHALKING condition. Penetrates and binds residual chalk layer to create adhesion surface for topcoat. Apply by spray_backroll or brush_roll per method. Full surface coverage — chalk layer is uniform across the elevation.
tasks.notes: RP-SPECIFIC primer path. Chalk-binding primer penetrates residual chalk that remains after rinse + chalk remediation. Full surface application — not spot. Most common FC siding RP primer scenario.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer — Spot Application on Exposed Bare FC
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon Masonry Primer or equivalent) to all exposed bare fiber cement areas where scraping removed paint to bare substrate. Bare FC is at pH 13.0 — standard latex primer will fail via saponification (alkaline burn of binder). Brush application to spot areas, feathering edges 2-3 inches onto surrounding sound paint.
tasks.notes: Critical RP primer path. Bare FC exposed by scraping requires alkali-resistant primer — same chemistry as NC SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT path (SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ALKALI). Spot application on scraped-to-bare areas, not full surface.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Full Prime Coat — Spray/Backroll Application
tasks.description: Apply full prime coat by spray_backroll. Sprayer leads, backroller follows immediately within wet edge to work primer into surface irregularities for maximum adhesion. 2-person operation. Primer product determined by substrate state: acrylic stain-block for general RP adhesion (SYS_EXT_FCRP_PRIMER_ACRYLIC_RP). Applied AFTER spot alkali-resistant primer on bare areas has cured.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Skip prime — verified adhesion, no bare areas

tasks.notes: Full surface prime over entire siding after spot alkali-resistant primer has cured. ~25% slower than NC spray-only due to backroll pass. 2-person crew.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_PRIME_SPRAY — spray_backroll replaces spray-only, state-driven primer selection

tasks.name: Full Prime Coat — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply full prime coat by brush and roller. Brush for edges and transitions, roller for open field. Fallback method for <750 SF, occupied-adjacent, or high wind. Primer product determined by substrate state (same selection as spray_backroll).
tasks.notes: Same method as NC brush/roll but RP primer is state-driven. Rate unchanged from NC.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_PRIME_BRUSH_ROLL — state-driven RP primer selection

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Chalk-binding primer (SS_EXT_CHALKING only) → OR → Spot alkali-resistant primer on bare FC areas → Allow spot prime to cure → Full surface acrylic stain-block prime (SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT / SS_EXT_PEELING). Module SKIPPED entirely when SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT with verified adhesion.

sop_modules.name: Finish Coat Application — Coat 1 and Coat 2 (Spray/Backroll Primary, Brush/Roll Fallback)
sop_modules.description: Combined finish coat module for both coat 1 and coat 2. spray_backroll is PRIMARY RP method (departure from NC spray-only — existing painted FC surface is no longer factory-smooth, benefits from backroll for adhesion into surface imperfections). brush_roll is fallback for <750 SF, occupied-adjacent, or high wind. QT2: single finish coat. QT3/QT4: two finish coats per Hardie warranty. Hardie-approved topcoat systems: QT2/QT3 standard (SW Duration or equivalent), QT4 premium (SW Emerald, BM Aura). Sheens: flat, satin.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray/Backroll Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by spray_backroll. Sprayer leads with even passes, backroller follows immediately within wet edge to work product into surface irregularities. 2-person operation. Consistent mil build, uniform coverage. spray_backroll provides superior adhesion on previously painted FC surfaces compared to spray-only.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No drips or holidays.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 6-10 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 6 ft.

tasks.notes: RP departure from NC spray-only: spray_backroll for adhesion on weathered existing paint film. ~25% slower than NC spray-only. Tip selection: 517 for lap/panel, 413 for shingle (same as NC). 519 tip option for failing/peeling surfaces with significant bare areas.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_FINISH_1_SPRAY — spray_backroll replaces spray-only

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by brush and roller. Fallback method for small projects <750 SF, occupied-adjacent areas, or high wind conditions. Brush for edges and transitions, roller for open field. Maintain wet edge to lap line.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. Consistent roller texture. Maintain wet edge to lap line.

tasks.notes: Same method as NC. Rate unchanged.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_FINISH_1_BRUSH_ROLL — re-keyed, unchanged method

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray/Backroll Application (QT3/QT4)
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by spray_backroll. Critical for appearance and film build. Same technique as coat 1. QT3/QT4 only — QT2 receives single finish coat.

quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 6 ft. Final appearance coat.

tasks.notes: Skipped at QT2. Second and final finish coat.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_FINISH_2_SPRAY — spray_backroll replaces spray-only

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush/Roll Application (QT3/QT4)
tasks.description: Apply second finish coat by brush and roller. Fallback method. QT3/QT4 only.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. No brush marks. Maintain wet edge to lap line. Final coat.

tasks.notes: Same method as NC. Rate unchanged. Skipped at QT2.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_FCSD_FINISH_2_BRUSH_ROLL — re-keyed, unchanged method

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Finish coat 1 → Interstage (MOD_FCRP_INTERSTAGE) → Finish coat 2 (QT3/QT4 only). QT2 receives single finish coat only. Allow recoat time per product TDS before interstage/coat 2.

sop_modules.name: Interstage Inspection, Sanding, and Touch-Up
sop_modules.description: Inspect first finish coat, touch up defects. Light sand at QT4 only. Module skipped for QT2 single-coat systems. Runs between finish coat 1 and finish coat 2.

tasks.name: Interstage Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect first finish coat for holidays, runs, sags, overspray on adjacent surfaces, and coverage defects. Check backroll texture uniformity.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays at 6-10 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic inspection at 6 ft viewing distance. Mark all visible defects.

tasks.notes: Direct transfer from NC. QT2 skipped (single coat).
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_INSPECT_COAT (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

tasks.name: Interstage Light Sand (QT4 Only)
tasks.description: Light sand between finish coats with 220 grit for mechanical adhesion. QT4 only — not required at QT3.

quality_notes.QT4: Light scuff sand. Remove nibs and defects. Uniform scratch pattern.

tasks.notes: Direct transfer from NC. QT4 only.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_SAND_BETWEEN (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

tasks.name: Interstage Touch-Up
tasks.description: Repair defects found during interstage inspection. Brush touch-up of holidays, runs, sags.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix all defects found during inspection. Blend repairs.

tasks.notes: Direct transfer from NC.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_TOUCHUP_REPAIR (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

tasks.name: Intercoat Dust Removal (QT4 Only)
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust before second coat. Tack cloth or compressed air.
tasks.notes: Direct transfer from NC. QT4 only — paired with interstage sand.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_DUST_INTERCOAT (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Sand (QT4 only) → Touch up → Dust removal → Coat 2. Module skipped for QT2 single-coat systems.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs after finish coat 1, before finish coat 2. Skipped for QT2 single-coat.

sop_modules.name: Final Inspection, Touch-Up, Protection Teardown, Equipment Cleanup, Site Cleanup, Customer Walkthrough
sop_modules.description: Combined cleanup module: final walkthrough inspection of completed siding finish per elevation, touch-up defects, protection material removal (landscape, hardscape, fixtures, HVAC, vehicle/driveway), equipment cleanup (flush sprayer, clean rollers/brushes), site debris cleanup, and customer walkthrough (RP-specific — occupied home, verify color/sheen/coverage per elevation with homeowner).

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all elevations and inspect finished siding for coverage, consistency, and defects. Check all adjacent surface protection for overspray transfer. Verify caulk joints are covered and consistent.

quality_notes.QT2: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for misses.
quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Check for holidays, runs, overspray on trim.
quality_notes.QT4: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. 6 ft viewing standard. All visible defects marked.

tasks.notes: Direct transfer from NC with RP addition: check caulk joints for coverage.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_FINAL_INSPECT (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

tasks.name: Final Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Blend repairs seamlessly.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft standard.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, HVAC covers, vehicle/driveway poly. Check for tape residue on all surfaces.
tasks.notes: Includes RP-specific vehicle/driveway protection removal. Check for tape residue. Remove all protection materials completely.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_PROTECT_TEARDOWN (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_, added vehicle/driveway zone)

tasks.name: Clean Equipment
tasks.description: Flush airless sprayer, clean tips and filters, coil hoses. Clean 18-inch backroll frames and roller covers. Clean brushes and rollers if used. RP adds backroll equipment cleanup.
tasks.notes: FIXED time per project. Full flush cycle for sprayer. Tips, filters, and backroll equipment cleaned and stored.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_CLEAN_EQUIPMENT (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

tasks.name: Site Debris Cleanup
tasks.description: Collect all debris — sandpaper, scraping debris, caulk tubes, tape, paint cans, biocide containers, roller covers. Leave site clean. RP generates more debris than NC due to scraping and caulk work.
tasks.notes: FIXED time per project. Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials and debris removed.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_FCSD_SITE_CLEANUP (re-keyed TSK_FCSD_ to TSK_FCRP_)

tasks.name: Customer Walkthrough (RP-Specific)
tasks.description: Post-completion review with homeowner. Walk each elevation together, verify color/sheen satisfaction, point out any areas of concern, document completion sign-off. RP-specific — occupied home context. NC does not include customer walkthrough (customer is GC/builder, not homeowner).
tasks.notes: RP-SPECIFIC. FIXED time per project (~15-20 min). Standard RP practice for occupied homes.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final inspection → Touch-up → Protection teardown → Equipment cleanup → Site debris cleanup → Customer walkthrough (last task on project).

sop_modules.name: Lead-Safe RRP Exterior Containment (Shared Module)
sop_modules.description: Shared exterior lead-safe RRP containment module. Conditional on pre_1978 = true. Per-elevation setup: 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure, lead screening test, wet scrape method, HEPA vacuum, containment teardown with lead-safe disposal. Shared across all exterior RP specs — do NOT duplicate containment tasks. RRP is very rare for FC siding (fiber cement introduced ~1987) but required for EPA compliance when the BUILDING is pre-1978.

tasks.name: Lead Screening Test (XRF or Swab)
tasks.description: Perform lead test at representative siding areas per elevation. XRF preferred; lead swab test acceptable. Test at minimum 2 locations per elevation. Results gate all subsequent RRP tasks and 2.0x prep modifier (FAC_FCRP_RRP).
tasks.notes: Shared task. Per-elevation FIXED time. FC siding was introduced ~1987 — most FC is post-1978, but building structure may be pre-1978 with replacement siding.
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

tasks.name: RRP Exterior Containment Setup (Per Elevation)
tasks.description: Install 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745. Secure edges with weights or stakes. Install warning signage. Restrict area to certified RRP personnel only. Per-elevation setup.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Per-elevation FIXED time. 6-mil poly minimum per EPA RRP Rule.
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

tasks.name: RRP Wet Scraping Method
tasks.description: Wet-scrape method for lead paint removal on siding. Mist surface with water before scraping to minimize dust generation. All scraping debris falls into containment below. EPA RRP requirement when disturbing lead paint. Applied as method override on TSK_FCRP_SCRAPE_FEATHER.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Applied per SF. RRP doubles prep time (2.0x modifier via FAC_FCRP_RRP).
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

tasks.name: HEPA Vacuum Lead Dust Cleanup
tasks.description: HEPA vacuum all surfaces and containment areas after scraping and sanding is complete. EPA RRP requirement — standard shop vac is NOT acceptable. Must achieve clearance standard before coating.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Applied per SF. HEPA vacuum is mandatory after all paint-disturbing activities in RRP.
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

tasks.name: RRP Containment Teardown and Lead-Safe Disposal
tasks.description: Fold containment poly inward to capture debris. Bag all lead-contaminated waste in 6-mil disposal bags. Label per EPA requirements. Per-elevation teardown.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Per-elevation FIXED time. All lead waste must be disposed per EPA hazardous waste regulations.
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Lead screen → Containment setup → (prep work with wet scrape method) → HEPA vacuum → Containment teardown. Entire module conditional on pre_1978 = true + lead-positive test result.

round_configurations.name: 2 Finish Coats Only (No Prime, GOOD Condition)
round_configurations.description: Skip prime when adhesion test passes on sound exterior paint with no bare areas. Cosmetic refresh or color change on well-maintained FC siding.
round_configurations.notes: Common RP scenario for sound-paint FC. Adhesion test MUST pass. No bare areas visible.

round_configurations.name: 1 Finish Coat Only (Economy QT2, GOOD Condition)
round_configurations.description: Economy single-coat FC siding RP on sound paint. Minimum viable scope.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy on already-sound paint. Minimum viable scope. Only appropriate on GOOD condition surfaces.

round_configurations.name: State-Driven Prime + 2 Finish Coats (FAIR/POOR Condition)
round_configurations.description: Standard RP round for FC siding with chalking, failing paint, or peeling. Prime coat is state-driven.
round_configurations.notes: Most common RP round for FAIR/POOR condition. Primer: chalk-binding (SS_EXT_CHALKING), acrylic stain-block + alkali-resistant on bare FC (SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT / SS_EXT_PEELING).

round_configurations.name: State-Driven Prime + 1 Finish Coat (Economy QT2, FAIR/POOR)
round_configurations.description: Economy RP with prime needed. Single finish coat on primed surface.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 budget scenario on degraded FC siding. Single finish coat.

module_sequence.notes: RRP containment (if applicable) after general setup but before assessment. Assessment drives prep/prime task activation. Rinse is first task in PREP. Caulk, clean, and final inspect merged into standard 8-module structure per user instruction (caulk → PREP, rinse/clean → PREP, final inspect → CLEANUP). Interstage runs between finish coat 1 and coat 2 (skipped for QT2). Elevation strategy: work one elevation at a time to minimize protection setup/teardown cycles.

assumptions.value: All NC DIRECT transfers re-keyed from TSK_FCSD_* to TSK_FCRP_* per RP convention
assumptions.source: User instruction: established RP convention (see SF_WINDOW_EXT_RP_v1 where TSK_XWIN_* to TSK_XWRP_*)
assumptions.note: Every task in the RP spec uses the FCRP prefix for consistency. Production.json must use TSK_FCRP_* IDs.

assumptions.value: spray_backroll is primary RP method (departure from NC spray-only)
assumptions.note: NC FC is spray-only (factory-smooth surface). RP FC uses spray_backroll because existing painted surface benefits from backroll for adhesion into surface imperfections.

assumptions.value: Low-pressure rinse only (400-600 PSI max) — power washing PROHIBITED on fiber cement
assumptions.note: CRITICAL departure from wood siding RP (1000-1500 PSI) and trim RP (500-1000 PSI). Damages embossed texture profiles, strips existing paint, forces water behind wall assembly.

assumptions.value: Caulk tasks merged into MOD_FCRP_PREP per user instruction (standard 8-module structure)
assumptions.source: User instruction: resolution proposed separate MOD_FCRP_CAULK, merged into PREP
assumptions.note: Resolution proposed 12 modules with separate CAULK, CLEAN, FINAL. Per user instruction: caulk → PREP, rinse/clean → PREP, final inspect → CLEANUP.

assumptions.value: Finish coat 1 and finish coat 2 merged into single MOD_FCRP_FINISH per user instruction
assumptions.source: User instruction: resolution proposed MOD_FCRP_FINISH_1 and MOD_FCRP_FINISH_2, merged into single FINISH
assumptions.note: Resolution proposed separate finish modules. Merged into single MOD_FCRP_FINISH containing all 4 finish tasks (coat 1 spray_backroll, coat 1 brush_roll, coat 2 spray_backroll, coat 2 brush_roll).

assumptions.value: Wind, sun, surface temp are NOT estimation modifiers — unpredictable at bid time
assumptions.note: Environmental conditions are SOP/scheduling concerns, not production rate modifiers.
